title.en: Two detained after French influencer's scorched body found in vineyard
title.zh: 法国影响者在葡萄园发现烧焦尸体后，两人被拘留

summary.en: Sonia Bellina's body was "abandoned" after "a murder of rare savagery", the family's lawyer says.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two men have been detained after a young woman's burned body was found in a vineyard in southern France, the local prosecutor has said.

In a statement on Wednesday, Nîmes prosecutor Cécile Gensac confirmed the body found in the Saint-Gilles vineyard belonged to social media influencer Sonia Bellina.

The 29-year-old had a following of around 260,000 on TikTok and was visiting her family in the area a month before her 30th birthday.

The two men were taken into police custody on Wednesday due to "evidence suggesting their direct or indirect involvement in the incident", the prosecutor said.

Police opened a murder investigation after a farmer found a body lying between rows of vines in the village near Nîmes on 12 August, but authorities did not confirm Bellina's identity for several days.

The prosecutor's initial assessment was that the body belonged to a young woman, but more tests were needed to confirm who it was.

In their latest update on Wednesday, Gensac said authorities could now confirm Bellina's identity after various investigations and DNA analysis.

She acknowledged that Bellina's name had been "widely circulated over the past 48 hours".

Prior to Gensac's update, the family's lawyer told French media that relatives were sure the body was Bellina's.

Mourad Battikh told broadcaster RTL the 29-year-old's body had been "abandoned" and "almost thrown away like garbage" in what he described as "a murder of rare savagery".

In the days since the scorched body was found, the identity and the circumstances of the death had sparked online speculation and rumours.

A woman who described herself as the influencer's sister - but did not share her name - said she was convinced the body found in the Saint-Gilles vineyard was her sister's before it was confirmed.

In an interview with the Midi Libre newspaper, she shared her family's ordeal and the harassment she says they have faced. According to her, some people have said Bellina "deserved what happened to her".

The family's lawyer has been firm in regards to online comments, saying he would "let nothing slide". Anything published would be subject to scrutiny and reported if necessary, Battikh said.

"The family is going through an extremely violent ordeal," he said in a press release, adding: "They request respect for their privacy and their grief and will not be making any further statements".
body.zh: 当地检察官表示，在法国南部的一个葡萄园里发现一名年轻女子被烧焦的尸体后，两名男子被拘留。 在周三的一份声明中，尼姆检察官塞西尔·让萨克证实，在圣吉尔葡萄园发现的尸体属于社交媒体影响者索尼娅·贝利娜。 这位 29 岁的女孩在 TikTok 上拥有约 26 万粉丝，在 30 岁生日前一个月她正在该地区探望家人。 检察官表示，由于“有证据表明他们直接或间接参与了这起事件”，这两名男子于周三被警方拘留。 8 月 12 日，一名农民在尼姆附近的村庄的一排葡萄藤之间发现了一具尸体，警方对此展开了谋杀调查，但当局几天来都没有确认贝利纳的身份。 检察官的初步评估是尸体属于一名年轻女子，但需要更多测试才能确认是谁。 Gensac 在周三的最新更新中表示，经过各种调查和 DNA 分析，当局现在可以确认贝利娜的身份。 她承认贝利娜的名字“在过去48小时内广泛流传”。 在根萨克发布最新消息之前，贝利娜家人的律师告诉法国媒体，亲属们确信尸体是贝利娜的。 穆拉德·巴蒂克 (Mourad Battikh) 告诉 RTL 广播公司，这名 29 岁的男子的尸体已被“遗弃”，“几乎像垃圾一样被扔掉”，他称这是“罕见的野蛮谋杀”。 自从这具烧焦的尸体被发现以来，死者的身份和死亡情况在网上引发了猜测和谣言。 一名自称是这位影响者妹妹的女士——但没有透露自己的名字——表示，在得到证实之前，她确信在圣吉尔葡萄园发现的尸体是她姐姐的。 在接受 Midi Libre 报纸采访时，她分享了家人的磨难和她所说的他们所面临的骚扰。据她说，有些人说贝利娜“活该”。 该家庭的律师对网上的评论态度坚决，称他“不会放过任何事情”。巴蒂克说，任何发布的内容都将受到审查，并在必要时进行报告。 他在一份新闻稿中说：“这个家庭正在经历极其暴力的磨难，”他补充道：“他们要求尊重他们的隐私和悲伤，并且不会发表任何进一步的声明。”

body.en: Mykhailo Fedorov’s blistering critique comes at a time of growing pressure for democratic renewal in Ukraine For more than a month, demonstrators have gathered in Ivan Franko Square outside Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s office. The protesters have been chanting a name – not that of Ukraine’s embattled president but that of the man he recently sacked as defence minister , Mykhailo Fedorov. On Sunday evening, 2,000 people marched along Khreshchatyk, Kyiv’s main boulevard, waving cardboard banners in support of their ousted hero. Zelenskyy has refused to reinstate Fedorov, who during his six months in the job was widely seen as an effective and reforming figure. On Wednesday, Ukraine’s parliament, the Rada, voted to approve a successor as defence minister, Yevhen Khmara. The move shows that Fedorov has been shut out from government permanently, and confirms his transition from trusted insider and Zelenskyy loyalist to a potent political opponent. Continue reading...

title.en: Israel opens up tenders for controversial West Bank settlement project
title.zh: 以色列对有争议的约旦河西岸定居点项目开放招标

summary.en: Plans to build on the so-called E1 area - east of Jerusalem - have long been internationally condemned and would in effect divide the occupied West Bank in two.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Israel has opened up tenders for the construction of some 1,200 settlement homes in a strategically important part of the occupied West Bank, as the government seeks to end any chance of a Palestinian state.

Plans to build on the so-called E1 area - east of Jerusalem - have long been internationally condemned.

The development would in effect divide the West Bank in two and isolate East Jerusalem.

The deadline for bids is days before Israel's October's general election , making it much harder for any future government to overturn any tenders issued.

Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem - land Palestinians want, along with Gaza, for a hoped-for future state - during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them.

Despite the fierce international opposition, successive Israeli governments have allowed settlements to grow.

However, expansion has risen sharply since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu returned to power in late 2022 at the head of a right-wing, pro-settler coalition, as well as the start of the Gaza war, triggered by Hamas's 7 October 2023 attack on Israel.

Under international pressure, Israel held off for decades on plans to build in E1.

Many of its allies and Palestinians argued these would deal a major blow to hopes of a two-state solution, effectively bisecting the West Bank.

But the current Israeli government gave the go-ahead for E1 construction a year ago, expressly to "erase" the idea of a Palestinian state.

Despite an Israeli court challenge to the plans by Bedouin Palestinians living in the area and Israeli peace groups, the housing ministry has now issued a tender for 1,234 of the 3,401 housing units approved by the Israeli government last August.

It covers about 12 sq km (4.6 sq miles) between East Jerusalem and the settlement of Maale Adumim

At the time of their unveiling, Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who is ultranationalist and settler, said the idea of a Palestinian state was "being erased".

The deadline for bids is 19 October, just days before Israel's general election on 27 October. That should enable the government to sign deals with contractors that it would be much harder for a future government to cancel.

Israel captured the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East War. It annexed East Jerusalem in 1980, in a move not recognised by the vast majority of the international community.

Opponents of the E1 project have warned that it would effectively block the establishment of a Palestinian state because it would cut off the north of the West Bank from the south, and prevent the development in the centre of a contiguous Palestinian urban area connecting Ramallah,...
body.zh: 以色列已公开招标，在被占领的约旦河西岸战略上重要的地区建造约 1,200 栋定居点房屋，政府试图终结巴勒斯坦建国的任何机会。 在耶路撒冷以东的所谓E1地区进行建设的计划长期以来一直受到国际社会的谴责。 这一发展实际上会将西岸一分为二，并孤立东耶路撒冷。 投标截止日期是以色列十月份大选的几天前，这使得未来的政府更难推翻任何已发布的投标。 自 1967 年中东战争期间占领约旦河西岸和东耶路撒冷以来，以色列已建造了约 160 个定居点，容纳了 70 万犹太人。巴勒斯坦人和加沙地带都希望这片土地能够建立一个充满希望的未来国家。据估计，有 330 万巴勒斯坦人与他们生活在一起。 尽管遭到国际社会的强烈反对，历届以色列政府还是允许定居点的扩张。 然而，自总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡于 2022 年底在右翼亲定居者联盟的领导下重新掌权以及哈马斯 2023 年 10 月 7 日袭击以色列引发加沙战争以来，扩张急剧增加。 在国际压力下，以色列推迟了数十年的 E1 建设计划。 其许多盟友和巴勒斯坦人认为，这将对两国解决方案的希望造成重大打击，实际上将约旦河西岸一分为二。 但以色列现任政府一年前就批准了E1建设，明确是为了“抹去”巴勒斯坦建国的想法。 尽管以色列法院对居住在该地区的贝都因巴勒斯坦人和以色列和平组织的计划提出质疑，但住房部现已对以色列政府去年 8 月批准的 3,401 套住房中的 1,234 套进行了招标。 它占地约 12 平方公里（4.6 平方英里），位于东耶路撒冷和 Maale Adumim 定居点之间 在它们揭幕时，极端民族主义者和定居者财政部长贝扎莱尔·斯莫特里奇表示，巴勒斯坦国的想法正在“被抹去”。 投标截止日期为 10 月 19 日，即 10 月 27 日以色列大选前几天。这将使政府能够与承包商签署协议，而未来的政府将更难取消这些协议。 1967年中东战争中，以色列从约旦手中夺取了包括东耶路撒冷在内的西岸地区。 1980年，它吞并了东耶路撒冷，此举并未得到国际社会绝大多数成员的认可。 E1项目的反对者警告说，该项目将有效阻止巴勒斯坦国的建立，因为它将切断西岸北部与南部的联系，并阻止连接拉马拉的邻近巴勒斯坦城市地区中心的开发。

title.en: Trump pauses new tariffs on Canada for three days, saying deal close
title.zh: 特朗普称交易已完成，暂停对加拿大征收新关税三天

summary.en: The US president says the two sides are finalising documents to avert import taxes targeting a range of Canadian goods.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump said he will delay imposing new tariffs on a wide array of Canadian goods for three days as the countries firm up a trade deal.

"I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for a three day period, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalization of documents, have a DEAL!" Trump said in a social media post.

The announcement came less than two hours before a 50% levy on nearly $20bn (£14.8bn; C$28bn) of Canadian imports was set to go in place.

The two sides have been at an impasse on several issues, including US tariffs on autos and many Canadian provinces banning American liquor sales.

Senior trade representatives for both countries met on Wednesday morning in Washington after Trump's tariff pause, indicating that discussions on a possible deal are still ongoing.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Trump characterised the deal as "very good" for both countries.

He suggested it would include concessions from Canada on agriculture and manufacturing, as well as a reduction of certain US tariffs on Canada.

Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke twice this week, and trade negotiators have been engaged in intense talks since July, after the US president threatened the new levy with a deadline of 19 August.

"Substantial progress has been made, although there is important work still to be done," Carney said in a letter posted on X.

In his post on Tuesday night, Trump also said a final trade deal could allow the revival of the Keystone XL pipeline. The oil pipeline, which would connect Alberta to the US, was blocked by both the Obama and Biden administrations.

Environmentalists and indigenous groups have long opposed the pipeline but Trump has said multiple times he would like to revive the project, which would carry 830,000 barrels of oil a day.

"The great Keystone XL Pipeline, long ago killed by Sleepy Joe Biden, may be awoken from the grave!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.

"The deal will include comprehensive market access for all American goods, economic security commitments, digital trade alignment", US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer's office posted on X.

It will also include "many important provisions that will continue to protect our market and American workers, along with our Canadian partners", it added.

Tuesday's extension is welcome news for Canadian negotiators and for businesses on both sides of the border, who have warned that the new tariffs would be harmful to both countries.

Tensions have mounted between the two major trading partners since Trump returned to office in January last year and he unleashed a wide-ranging global programme of tariffs, upending decades of free trade between Canada and the US.

summary.en: Senator Jon Ossoff, who is up for re-election, came up with arguably the standout line of the midterm elections so far Hello there, Jon Ossoff really struck a nerve. That much is clear. Continue reading...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US senator for Georgia, running for re-election in November, came up with arguably the standout line of the midterm elections campaign so far when discussing Donald Trump at a rally on Sunday.

“While the sailors on the [USS Abraham] Lincoln fight his war, while he fruitlessly drains our munitions and oil reserves, the president sleeps through his meetings. He golfs and trades stocks,” said Ossoff. “See, he doesn’t want to do the job.

“He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar.”

Not only did the remark enter into national consciousness the existence of ‘Natalie’ – Natalie Harp, the 35-year-old aide to Trump who rarely leaves the president’s side – Ossoff’s riff also succeeded in upsetting Steven Cheung, Trump’s director of communications.

“Jon Jackoff”, Cheung wrote on X on Monday, misspelling, perhaps deliberately, the name ‘Ossoff’, “has to be the biggest cuck loser in politics. Instead of denigrating hard working people serving their country, Jon should look deep into his soul and ask himself why he’s a miserable person who hates this country. It’s because he’s a radical, extremist Dumocrat.”

Even for someone in Trump’s orbit, where outbursts against political opponents are commonplace, this plumbed new lows. What could possibly have triggered Trump’s stoutly built, middle-aged communications guru into attacking Ossoff, the handsome, athletic, 39-year-old senator?

It’s hard to be sure. But, apropos of nothing, this essay by Dana Schwartz, from 2016, examined why rightwing men are obsessed with calling people “cucks”:

“‘Cuck’ is a concept borne [sic] out of insecurity: a fear that one is inadequate, sexually or otherwise, and that inadequacy will lead to the loss of the things that are important to him,” Schwartz wrote.

In any case, Trump wasn’t far behind Cheung, calling Ossoff a “Pee-wee Herman lookalike” – a reference to a TV and film character whose popularity peaked 40 years ago. (Trump has also called Ossoff “Pinky Herman” , which is neither a character nor a thing.)

The anonymous White House Rapid Response X account joined in too, branding a CNN reporter who had asked Trump about Ossoff a “disgraceful, humiliating embarrassment to her alleged profession”, and later posting :

“Someday, your children will come across your disgusting and inhumane question. They will be sickened and embarrassed to have a parent be so callous and vindictive. It’s quite troubling.”

It’s hard to really be shocked by any of this any more, with daily attacks on the media from the president and his most senior aides, but an official White House account, with 2.2 million followers, invoking a reporter’s children prompted widespread criticism.

title.en: Israel confirms soldiers fired at car in which Hind Rajab was killed and opens criminal investigation

summary.en: The five-year old Gaza girl initially survived the attack and pleaded for help but her body was recovered later with those of six of her relatives.

body.en:
The Israeli military has confirmed for the first time that it opened fire on a car carrying five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab, who was killed along with six relatives in Gaza in 2024.

Rajab initially survived the attack and answered a telephone call during which she pleaded for help. The call lasted hours.

An ambulance sent to reach her – in a move co-ordinated with the Israeli army - was then shelled, killing two paramedics. Hind's body was recovered days later, along with the others killed.

In a statement, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that it would open a criminal investigation into Hind and her family's killing, as well as the killing of 15 Palestinians, including medics and a UN worker, in March 2025.

The IDF said of the killing of Hind: "Due to alleged failures in the co-ordination of the movement of the Palestine Red Crescent ambulance, it has been decided to initiate a criminal investigation of the incident by Military Police Criminal Investigation Division."

It added that the findings of its examination "indicate that IDF troops fired at a vehicle" that was "travelling contrary to the advanced notice that had been published in an announcement by the IDF Spokesperson to residents of the area".

The IDF initially stated that none of its troops were in the area at the time of Hind's killing. However, that suggestion was soon questioned.

The IDF later said it had "conducted raids on terror targets" with forces operating in neighbourhoods in Gaza City, including Tel al-Hawa, where Hind was located.

Hind's killing was internationally condemned after a desperate recording of her speaking to paramedics of the Palestinian Red Crescent Society (PRCS) was broadcast around the world.

The sound of Hind's fragile voice on the other of the line that day haunted the Red Crescent operators long after her death, as she described seeing tanks directly in front of the car, moving towards her.

Operator Rana Faqih stayed on the line with Hind for hours, as the Red Crescent team appealed to the Israeli army to allow their ambulance to access the location.

Faqih said the child appealed to her over and over again for someone to come and rescue her.

"At one point, she told me it was getting dark," Rana told the BBC in February 2024. "She was scared. She asked me how far away my house was. I felt paralysed and helpless."

Three hours after the call began, an ambulance was finally cleared to approach the area, and was despatched to rescue Hind.

It was after dark when the crew - Yusuf al-Zeino and Ahmed al-Madhoun - notified operators that they were nearing the location, and were about to be checked for entry by Israeli forces.

title.en: India 'Cockroach' movement takes aim at government schools
title.zh: 印度“蟑螂”运动剑指政府学校

summary.en: A student protest movement in India, dubbed the 'Cockroach' movement, is expanding its grassroots efforts into a nationwide campaign. The initiative aims to audit government schools that have been neglected and to pressure authorities to address these issues.
summary.zh: 印度一项名为“蟑螂”的学生抗议运动正将其基层网络发展为全国性行动。该运动旨在审计被忽视的公立学校，并向当局施压，要求其采取行动。

body.en:
The student protest movement is turning its grassroots network into a nationwide campaign to audit neglected government schools and pressure authorities to act.

The student protest movement in India known as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) scored a major victory in July after Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down following weeks of demonstrations in Delhi.

Now, the movement is aiming its campaign for accountability at improving India's government schools.

Last week on India's Independence Day, the CJP launched a nationwide campaign asking citizens to inspect government schools, document what is missing and pressure local authorities to fix basic facilities.

Dubbed "Fix the Schools," the campaign aims to mobilize citizens to identify problems locally and make them public.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke launched a campaign in the Indian state of Maharashtra from his native village in Hingoli district. He spoke with students and documented what he said were broken windows, lack of clean drinking water, missing classroom benches and unusable bathrooms.

"No matter which political party ruled, nobody worked for government schools in states. Now there is a need, and we can make them work by asking questions," said Dipke.

Government officials did not respond to DW's requests for comment on the CJP's accusations.

The CJP has prepared assessment forms that parents, students and residents can use to document issues with local government schools. They are being asked to record video evidence, complete the assessment and send the material to CJP.

The organization plans to compile the reports into a public record of neglected schools and use them to pressure local authorities to respond.

The CJP has said the campaign will focus on five basic requirements: functioning toilets, electricity, clean drinking water, classroom benches and the quality of midday meals.

One element is to publicly recognize village heads who improve their local schools. The CJP plans to use before-and-after evidence to highlight villages where conditions have improved.

The organization has set an initial target of auditing at least 100 rural government schools over the next two months and pressing authorities to act on the findings.

title.en: Why the US is going after the International Criminal Court
title.zh: 美国为何追查国际刑事法院

summary.en: Marco Rubio, Donald Trump's secretary of state, has announced sanctions against two members of the International Criminal Court, including its president. Rubio's pressure on the court has far-reaching consequences.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Marco Rubio, Donald Trump's secretary of state, has announced sanctions against two members of the International Criminal Court, including its president. Rubio's pressure on the court has far-reaching consequences.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took aim at the International Criminal Court (ICC)  on Tuesday, calling it "corrupt and fatally politicized" and claiming it has "maliciously abused its authority and exceeded its mandate."

He announced sanctions against the ICC president, Tomoko Akane of Japan, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye of Senegal. The sanctions include freezing of their US-held bank assets and largely cutting them off from the US financial system.

The ICC has been holding individuals accountable for war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity since 2002. The court is based in  The Hague , just like the  International Court of Justice (ICJ) , which is part of the United Nations and settles disputes between states.

Unlike the ICJ, the ICC has 125 members, not all 193 UN member states. The US, Russia and China are among the countries that have not joined, along with several states in Asia and North Africa.

Rubio  had recently threatened to dismantle the court "brick by brick." In a statement in July, the State Department outlined a number of measures Washington is considering as part of its campaign against the court. These include visa restrictions on ICC staff and tougher sanctions targeting the court and affiliated organizations. It also suggested increased scrutiny of countries "that refuse to reject the ICC's illegitimate authority" while continuing to receive US assistance.

The US has clashed with the ICC before . But legal experts around the world say Washington's latest escalation marks a significant shift.

"What the US and Marco Rubio have now essentially done is make public something that has been going on for more than a year," Andreas Schüller, co-director of the International Crimes and Legal Accountability Program at the European Center for Constitutional and Human Rights (ECCHR) in Berlin, told DW in July.

"The US has been using various forms of diplomatic pressure against other countries in an effort to change their positions, and in some cases their voting behavior, toward the ICC," he added.

"The fact that it is now being declared a campaign shows that it is being pursued strategically, that it is broader in scope, and that other countries — including those that are not ICC members — are also being brought on board to help apply pressure."

body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的国务卿马可·卢比奥宣布对国际刑事法院的两名成员实施制裁，其中包括法院院长。卢比奥对球场的压力产生了深远的影响。 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥周二将矛头指向国际刑事法院（ICC），称其“腐败且致命的政治化”，并声称其“恶意滥用权力并超越其职权范围”。 他宣布对国际刑事法院主席、日本的茜智子和塞内加尔的高级审判律师阿卜杜拉耶·塞耶实施制裁。制裁包括冻结他们在美国持有的银行资产，并在很大程度上切断他们与美国金融体系的联系。 自 2002 年以来，国际刑事法院一直追究犯有战争罪、种族灭绝罪和反人类罪的个人的责任。该法院设在海牙，就像国际法院 (ICJ) 一样，国际法院是联合国的一部分，负责解决国家之间的争端。 与国际法院不同的是，国际刑事法院有 125 个成员国，而不是全部 193 个联合国成员国。 美国、俄罗斯和中国以及亚洲和北非的几个国家都没有加入。 卢比奥最近威胁要“一砖一瓦”地拆除法院。在 7 月份的一份声明中，国务院概述了华盛顿正在考虑采取的一系列措施，作为其针对该法院的行动的一部分。其中包括对国际刑事法院工作人员的签证限制以及针对法院及其附属组织的更严厉制裁。它还建议加强对“拒绝拒绝国际刑事法院非法权威”同时继续接受美国援助的国家的审查。 美国此前曾与国际刑事法院发生过冲突。但世界各地的法律专家表示，华盛顿最近的升级标志着一个重大转变。 柏林欧洲宪法与人权中心(ECCHR)国际犯罪和法律责任项目联席主任安德烈亚斯·舒勒(Andreas Schüller)7月份对德国之声表示：“美国和卢比奥现在所做的基本上就是将已经发生一年多的事情公之于众。” 他补充说：“美国一直在对其他国家利用各种形式的外交压力，试图改变他们对国际刑事法院的立场，甚至在某些情况下改变他们的投票行为。” “事实上，现在它被宣布为一场运动，这表明它是在战略上进行的，范围更广泛，而且其他国家——包括非国际刑事法院成员国——也被拉上来帮助施加压力。” 美国不是国际刑事法院的成员，这意味着在美国境内犯下的罪行不属于其管辖范围。但国际刑事法院可以起诉成员国内涉嫌犯下的暴行——这一原则……

title.en: Pakistan: Could ex-PM Imran Khan make a new deal?
title.zh: 巴基斯坦：前总理伊姆兰·汗能否达成新协议？

summary.en: The imprisoned former prime minister of Pakistan was moved to a hospital for medical treatment, ushering speculation over the possibility of new political negotiations.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The imprisoned former prime minister of Pakistan was moved to a hospital for medical treatment, ushering speculation over the possibility of new political negotiations.

Pakistan's Supreme Court on Tuesday ordered jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan to be shifted to a private hospital after Khan's family and political supporters repeatedly raised concerns about the 73 year old's deteriorating health in Rawalpindi's Adiala jail. 

The founder of the opposition party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) has been imprisoned since August 2023 and is currently serving a 14-year sentence on corruption charges he says are politically motivated.

The former prime minister was ousted in a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022. Khan and his supporters say Pakistan's influential military is trying to keep him out of politics, an allegation the military denies.

Despite his remaining behind bars, Khan remains politically popular. Despite a crackdown on the PTI following Khan's arrest, the candidates backed by him performed strongly in the February 2024 elections.

"Three years in prison have not removed Khan from Pakistani politics. He remains PTI's biggest political asset, but the party's reliance on him has also exposed weaknesses in its leadership and organization," Raza Rumi, a US-based Pakistani political analyst, told DW.

The transfer of Khan to the Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for medical assessment has added a new dimension to the debate over his future and the possibility of political negotiations.

However, Khan's adviser Sayed Zulfi Bukhari rejected speculation that court decision was the result of any political deal with the government.

"There is no deal between Imran Khan and anyone. This is the Supreme Court's decision, which is very much welcomed," Bukhari said.

Pakistan's Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said in a video statement issued on Tuesday night that the government would challenge the Supreme Court order , claiming it was unlawful.

The minister said a convicted prisoner must be treated inside the jail or at a public hospital according to law, adding that he was requesting Khan's medical tests be carried out at a government hospital instead of a private facility.

"Legally, Khan has not been granted bail nor have his convictions been suspended. He will remain a prisoner, and the hospital executive ward shall serve as a sub-jail. Unfortunately, most ordinary prisoners with far more serious ailments are never allowed such facilities by the courts," Osama Malik, a legal expert, told DW. 

Pakistan's Minister of State for Interior, Talal Chaudhry, told DW that "Khan's cases will be decided by the courts."

body.zh: 被监禁的巴基斯坦前总理被转移到医院接受治疗，引发了人们对新政治谈判可能性的猜测。 巴基斯坦最高法院周二下令将被监禁的前总理伊姆兰·汗转移到一家私立医院，此前汗的家人和政治支持者多次对这位 73 岁的前总理伊姆兰·汗在拉瓦尔品第阿迪亚拉监狱中健康状况恶化表示担忧。 反对党巴基斯坦正义运动 (PTI) 创始人自 2023 年 8 月以来一直被监禁，目前正在服刑 14 年，罪名是他所说的出于政治动机的腐败指控。 这位前总理在 2022 年 4 月的议会不信任投票中被赶下台。汗和他的支持者表示，巴基斯坦有影响力的军方正试图让他远离政治，但军方否认了这一指控。 尽管汗仍在狱中，但他在政治上仍然很受欢迎。尽管汗被捕后 PTI 遭到打压，但他支持的候选人在 2024 年 2 月的选举中表现强劲。 驻美国的巴基斯坦政治分析人士拉扎·鲁米 (Raza Rumi) 告诉德国之声：“三年监禁并没有将汗从巴基斯坦政治中剔除。他仍然是巴基斯坦正义党最大的政治资产，但该党对他的依赖也暴露了其领导和组织方面的弱点。” 汗被转移到伊斯兰堡希法国际医院接受医疗评估，这为有关他的未来和政治谈判可能性的争论增添了新的维度。 然而，汗的顾问赛义德·祖尔菲·布哈里否认了法院判决是与政府达成任何政治协议的结果的猜测。 “伊姆兰·汗和任何人之间都没有达成协议。这是最高法院的决定，非常受欢迎，”布哈里说。 巴基斯坦法律部长阿扎姆·纳齐尔·塔拉尔在周二晚发布的视频声明中表示，政府将对最高法院的命令提出质疑，声称该命令是非法的。 该部长表示，根据法律，被定罪的囚犯必须在监狱或公立医院接受治疗，并补充说，他要求汗的医学检查在政府医院而不是私人机构进行。 法律专家奥萨马·马利克（Osama Malik）告诉德国之声：“从法律上讲，汗没有获得保释，他的定罪也没有被暂停。他仍将是囚犯，医院的行政病房将作为分监狱。不幸的是，大多数患有严重疾病的普通囚犯都不会被法院允许使用此类设施。” 巴基斯坦内政部长塔拉勒·乔杜里 (Talal Chaudhry) 告诉德国之声，“汗的案件将由法院裁决。” PTI 的布哈里告诉德国之声，汗“在……期间没有得到正确的医疗护理”。

title.en: Fact check: How do I spot fake social media accounts, bots and trolls?
title.zh: 事实核查：如何发现虚假社交媒体帐户、机器人和巨魔？

summary.en: If you are unsure whether to trust a message on TikTok or X, study its source. The following indicators can help you determine if you are dealing with a fake account, bot or troll.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 如果您不确定是否信任 TikTok 或 X 上的消息，请研究其来源。以下指标可以帮助您确定您是否正在与虚假帐户、机器人或巨魔打交道。 数十万个不真实​​的社交媒体帐户。数以万计的假文章。数以百万计的自动帖子。 这些是德国外交部引用的一些与俄罗斯虚假信息活动有关的数据，该活动于 2022 年俄罗斯入侵乌克兰后首次被发现。 该行动被称为“Doppelgänger”，旨在放大德国等国家社交媒体平台上的亲俄言论。 该部在 2024 年的一份报告中表示，在某些日子里，数千个账户处于活跃状态，以协调的方式每秒发布一次以上。 此活动强调了用户验证社交媒体帐户的真实性并识别内容何时被机器人和巨魔发布或放大的重要性。 但首先，机器人和巨魔之间有什么区别？你如何发现它们？ DW 事实检查提供了一些提示来帮助您驾驭当今的信息格局。 虚假帐户是隐藏其真实身份的社交媒体资料。有些可能会冒充普通用户；其他人可以冒充政客、机构或记者。 并非所有虚假帐户都有恶意。有些人可能会使用假名来保护自己的身份或出于安全原因。活动人士或举报人可能会使用虚假帐户来调查敏感问题。 机器人（机器人的简称）不知疲倦地评论帖子、分享内容，或人为地引发关于边缘或其他被忽视主题的在线辩论。有时，他们完全是无辜的，但有时他们的意图是有害的。 好的机器人可以自动在社交媒体上分享新闻或天气预报，以及地震警报和卫星图像。 相比之下，坏机器人旨在模仿真正的人类活动以推进特定议程。 根据算法的不同，此类计算机程序可以撰写和发布社交媒体帖子或评论、关注他人，甚至发送好友请求。 坏机器人可以通过在社交媒体平台上放大某些政治观点并人为地引起对某些问题的关注来扭曲现实。 另一方面，巨魔是真实的人类，他们表现出破坏性和过度活跃的在线行为。 有些人甚至受雇骚扰某些公众人物或媒体组织，作为所谓的巨魔工厂或农场的一部分。 巨魔工厂最突出的例子之一是俄罗斯圣彼得堡的互联网研究机构。 EUvsDisinfo 是欧洲的一个项目...

title.en: 'Power of the purse': What Trump stands to lose in US midterm test
title.zh: “钱袋子”的力量：特朗普在美国中期选举中可能失去什么

summary.en: As midterm primaries continue with elections in several states this week, analysts are predicting a shake-up in the political landscape, indicating potential shifts in influence for former President Trump.
summary.zh: 随着本周几个州中期初选的继续进行，分析人士预测政治格局将发生变化，预示着前总统特朗普的影响力可能出现转变。

body.en:
The 2026 United States midterm elections will be a crucial test of Donald Trump's political strength, with Democrats hoping to regain control of Congress and Republicans seeking to defy the historical tendency for a president's party to lose ground halfway through a term.

The November elections will determine control of the House of Representatives and could reshape the balance of power in Washington for the final two years of Trump's presidency.

The first midterm primaries were held in March and have continued in recent months, with Alaska, Florida and Wyoming holding their primaries this week.

For Democrats, the November midterms offer an opportunity to demonstrate that dissatisfaction with Trump can translate into electoral gains and to begin rebuilding the party ahead of the next general election in 2028.

For Republicans, the elections will test whether Trump's political strength remains sufficient to protect the party from the historical midterm backlash that has affected many previous administrations.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

And for Trump himself, a Democratic-controlled House could mean substantially greater scrutiny, investigations and political resistance during the final years of his presidency.

Wesley Widmaier, a professor at the Australian National University Department of International Relations, told SBS News an overall loss for Trump would restrict his influence.

"The House controls the power of the purse and is where budgets originate in the American system. A Democrat win would mean a loss of a lot of control for Trump," he said.

Ultimately, the midterms could provide the clearest indication yet of whether the political momentum in the US is shifting away from Trump and the Republican Party — or whether Republicans can defy the historical pattern and maintain their grip on Congress.

Every two years, US citizens elect all 435 members of the House of Representatives, while roughly one-third of the Senate is elected.

The House of Representatives has the special power to initiate tax bills and to impeach officials, while the Senate approves presidential appointments, such as judges and cabinet members.

Unlike in Australia, voting in US elections is not compulsory, and midterm elections — those held between presidential elections — tend to have lower voter turnout and less media attention.

title.en: Donald Trump says no Iran talks planned, shares map showing Hormuz as 'new US territory'
title.zh: 特朗普称未计划与伊朗谈判，并分享地图将霍尔木兹海峡标为“美国新领土”

summary.en: US President Donald Trump stated that no talks with Iran are planned, while also sharing a map that depicted the Strait of Hormuz as "new US territory." Iran has maintained its stance that it will not reopen the vital waterway unless the US lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，目前没有与伊朗进行谈判的计划，同时他还分享了一张地图，将霍尔木兹海峡标注为“美国新领土”。伊朗坚称，除非美国解除对伊朗港口的封锁，否则不会重新开放这条重要的航道。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has said no talks with Iran are underway and none are scheduled, as he posted a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as a new US territory.

Trump has been pressing his threat to claim sovereignty over the crucial energy waterway as the nearly six-month-old Iran war grinds on with little sign of resolution.

Trump's envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner had said on Monday that the US and Iran were having "very positive and active conversations", but the president denied that was the case.

"There are no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled, with the Islamic Republic of Iran. The Naval Blockade remains in full force and effect," Trump wrote on his Truth Social network on Tuesday night.

"The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. All water mines have been removed or detonated."

US sources told the Agence-France Presse news agency there had been "positive" discussions with the Iranians, but added that Trump had decided to wait and asked his team not to engage until Iran was ready to make a deal.

In recent weeks, there has been a lull in fighting, though the United Arab Emirates has recently accused Iran of firing two ballistic missiles — which landed at sea — targeting "maritime navigation." Iran, however, denied firing a missile toward the UAE.

Soon after, the UAE announced that "in light of regional escalations" it was halting all trade, commercial exchanges and financial transactions with Iran.

The UAE bore the brunt of Iranian missile and drone attacks in the first period of the war, but had not reported any attacks since the US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that was meant to halt the fighting.

Earlier on Tuesday, Trump posted a map on Truth Social showing the Strait of Hormuz as a "NEW U.S. Territory".

Iran has effectively shut down the chokepoint , through which a fifth of the world's oil would usually transit, in retaliation for the war launched by the US and Israel in late February.

Trump revisited the idea again earlier in the week in comments to reporters in the Oval Office.

This is not the first time that Trump, faced with a foreign policy obstacle, has threatened to annex foreign territory.

Since returning to power in 2025, he has threatened to make Canada the 51st US state, seize Greenland and Cuba, and has even alluded to taking control of the Gaza Strip, without following through on any of these threats.

Before the Iran war erupted on 28 February, the Strait of Hormuz was an open waterway with free passage.

title.en: Designed to 'exploit' children: Meta faces a historic courtroom reckoning
title.zh: 旨在“剥削”儿童：Meta 面临历史性的法庭审判

summary.en: The trial's outcome could help reshape Facebook and Instagram, and leave Meta with billions of dollars to pay in penalties.

body.en:
Meta knowingly hooked and exploited children, a United States federal court has heard in the trial of the social media giant on charges that it deliberately made Instagram and Facebook addictive to young users.

In what many experts have called social media's "big tobacco moment," a coalition of US states is demanding Meta pay US$200 billion ($282 billion) in penalties for using technology specifically designed to foster addiction among children in a similar fashion to cigarettes.

Meta "exploited how kids' brains work," California prosecutor Megan O'Neill said in opening arguments, painting Meta's business model as one built to "hook the users, hold them for as long as they can, harvest their data, and then hide the truth from the public".

"It worked especially well for kids," O'Neill added. "Meta needed kids, and it needed to reassure the people who cared about those kids that the kids are safe."

Meta's lawyer, Paul Schmidt, acknowledged that some users were harmed by the networks, but argued that the company had "tried to come up with tools to help them". He argued research showed no clear link between adolescents' social media use and a lack of well-being.

He also said Mark Zuckerberg, Meta's co-founder and CEO, shared the company's desire to improve its services, and not make them dangerous.

"They don't believe they're going to do well if people don't like their service," Schmidt said.

Before the trial began, the company denied all the allegations, insisting it had worked with parents, experts and law enforcement to incorporate protective safeguards for children.

This is not the first case seeking to hold tech companies — including Meta — accountable for these types of issues, but it could become one of the most consequential if it leads to sweeping changes on the platforms.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify, along with Instagram head Adam Mosseri.

Activists, including mothers of children they say were driven to suicide by their social media usage, rallied outside court.

One mother, Lori Schott, called out Zuckerberg and Mosseri, saying they "built one of those most powerful and richest companies in the world... But power does not excuse harm."

This is the first federal trial in what is expected to be a tidal wave of lawsuits also targeting TikTok, Snapchat and YouTube as families, educators and state governments charge them with harming the mental health of young people.

Meta, which has more than three billion users worldwide, is the sole defendant in this case.

body.en:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo’s fast-moving Ebola outbreak has now killed over 2,300 people and become the deadliest outbreak of the disease on record in the Central African nation.

The outbreak unfolding in one of DRC's most vulnerable regions is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever, with 4,945 cases including 2,325 deaths, according to government data.

It's the DRC's 17th outbreak, with a toll that has eclipsed that of the country's 2018-2020 outbreak when 2,299 deaths out of 3,481 cases were recorded.

The latest data shows 101 new cases and 33 deaths reported in the previous 24 hours. Over 1,000 people have recovered, while 730 remain in hospitals or isolation.

The outbreak has infected and killed more people at a greater speed than any other outbreak in history. The World Health Organization has said it is on track to surpass the 2014-16 Ebola outbreak in West Africa, the deadliest on record with more than 11,000 deaths.

Trish Newport, emergency coordinator with Doctors Without Borders, said the limited community engagement in the outbreak remains a key challenge.

"The community needs to be aware about the outbreak," she told The Associated Press news agency, adding that people "need to be involved in the response, and they need to know what the signs and symptoms are and what to do if they get sick. And this today is not happening in every single place where there are Ebola cases".

Starting from the first confirmed case, the outbreak reached 2,000 killed almost three times faster than in the 2014-16 outbreak.

Some families have lost up to 15 of their relatives in the epicentre, the Ituri province, Newport said.

"We rapidly need to scale up to be able to prevent more deaths from happening, more families and communities from being impacted," she added.

There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the rare Bundibugyo virus responsible for the current outbreak across six provinces in Congo's east. Trials for those are ongoing in Ituri.

Most new cases and deaths are being reported outside of the people being monitored. Challenges facing medical teams dealing with the outbreak also include strikes by some unpaid health workers, threats by rebel groups, anger from long-traumatised communities, bad roads making it difficult to reach all the affected territories, and misinformation claiming that Ebola isn’t real.

The WHO warned over the weekend that the outbreak is still moving at an "exceptional pace" ahead of efforts to track it, noting that it reached a weekly record of 579 cases and 304 deaths in the previous week.

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼与中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia's participation in a limited naval exercise with China near Taiwan has raised questions about its long-standing nonaligned foreign policy.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚与中国海军在台湾附近举行了有限的海上演习，这引发了对其长期不结盟外交政策的担忧。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan.

body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

reflection.en: In a world of complex geopolitical dynamics, nations often strive to maintain peace and neutrality. Indonesia's efforts to navigate its foreign policy amidst regional tensions reflect the ongoing challenge of living at peace with all, as far as it depends on them. This pursuit requires wisdom and a steadfast commitment to de-escalation and understanding.
reflection.zh: 在复杂的地缘政治格局中，各国常努力维持和平与中立。印度尼西亚在区域紧张局势中努力调整其外交政策，反映了在力所能及的范围内与所有人和平相处的持续挑战。这种追求需要智慧和对缓和局势、增进理解的坚定承诺。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: After Hormuz, China looks to the promise – and peril – of the Arctic’s ‘ice silk road’
title.zh: 继霍尔木兹海峡之后，中国着眼于北极“冰上丝绸之路”的机遇与风险

summary.en: China has initiated the first regular shipping transits through the Arctic's northern sea route, aiming to establish an "ice silk road." This new maritime path, however, raises significant concerns regarding its potential environmental impact and geopolitical implications.
summary.zh: 中国已开通北极航线的首次定期运输，旨在建立一条“冰上丝绸之路”。然而，这条新的海上航线在环境影响和地缘政治方面引发了重大担忧。

body.en: China has established the first scheduled transit through the northern sea route, but questions remain over the environmental and political risks When Marco Rubio suggested that the world should look to new shipping lanes to bypass the logjammed strait of Hormuz, it’s unlikely he had the Arctic’s northern sea route in mind. And yet in recent months the promise of this 5,500km channel – cleaved through frozen seas by nuclear-powered icebreakers and illuminated by a sun that never dips below the Arctic horizon – has grown. Continue reading...
body.zh: 中国已经建立了第一条通过北方海路的定期过境航线，但环境和政治风险仍然存在问题。当马可·卢比奥建议世界应该寻求新的航道以绕过堵塞的霍尔木兹海峡时，他不太可能想到北极的北方海路。然而近几个月来，这条 5,500 公里长的航道 — — 由核动力破冰船劈开冰冻的海洋，并由永远不会低于北极地平线的太阳照亮 — — 的前景越来越大。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The pursuit of new trade routes like the Arctic's "ice silk road" highlights humanity's drive for progress and efficiency. Yet, as the story notes, such ventures also carry significant environmental and political risks that demand careful consideration. Yahweh's wisdom encourages us to foresee danger and take precautions, rather than rushing headlong into...
reflection.zh: 像北极“冰上丝绸之路”这样的新贸易路线的开辟，彰显了人类对进步和效率的追求。然而，正如报道所指出的，此类项目也伴随着重大的环境和政治风险，需要我们审慎考量。雅伟的智慧鼓励我们预见危险并采取预防措施，而不是为了短期利益而贸然陷入潜在的危机。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

Yahweh's word reminds us that truth ultimately prevails, and deceit cannot endure indefinitely.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻揭示了欺骗，即使精心策划，也往往寿命有限。虚假信息可能一时蒙蔽，但其真实面目终将被揭露，正如这些虚假网站被查获一样。雅伟的话语提醒我们，真理最终会得胜，谎言无法永远持续。

verse.textZh: 口吐真言，永远坚立；舌说谎话，只存片时。

body.en: Boats carrying hundreds of people are a clear and alarming trend. But where do such large vessels come from? Providing a large dinghy for use in the choppy seas of western Europe was not a problem, as long as the order was for more than 20 vessels, they said. The sales manager at the Chinese company even had an online brochure for an undercover Guardian reporter, posing as a prospective client, to peruse. They had a production capacity of 500 boats a month and, yes, it was possible to get even bigger ones for the right price. They could do a seven or even an eight-metre military-style dinghy for $1,678 (£1,238) a boat, without the engines, but that would be lacking CE certification, the mandatory mark that shows a product meets EU health and safety requirements. Additional reporting by Lyndon Li Continue reading...

reflection.en: This report on the supply of vessels for perilous journeys reminds us of the vulnerable individuals seeking safety and new beginnings. Yahweh calls us to recognize His presence in those who are marginalized and in desperate need. Our compassion for 'the least of these' reflects our love for Him.
reflection.zh: 这篇关于用于危险旅程的船只供应的报道，提醒我们那些寻求安全和新生活的弱势个体。雅伟呼召我们要在那些被边缘化和极度需要的人身上认出祂的存在。我们对“这些最小的弟兄”的怜悯，反映了我们对祂的爱。

verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: 'Left feeling like a burden': How the government's new NDIS changes may impact you
title.zh: “感到自己是负担”：政府新的NDIS改革可能如何影响你

summary.en: The National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) in Australia is undergoing changes, prompting concerns that these reforms may lead some participants to feel like a burden.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚的国家残疾保险计划（NDIS）即将进行改革，引发了人们的担忧，认为这些变化可能让一些参与者感到自己成为负担。

body.en:
An overhaul of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) has passed the Senate with Coalition support, sent back to the Labor-controlled lower house to be rubber-stamped.

Analysis by the Grattan Institute suggests hundreds of thousands of people will be moved off the scheme or prevented from joining under the changes.

Applicants will be assessed in stages under a new test to determine their functional capacity.

That test is still being developed and will replace the current diagnosis-based model.

Acting CEO of peak body People With Disability Australia Megan Spindler-Smith says her community is grieving.

"There will be harm, there will be injuries. What we're talking about here is that when you reduce people's access to the supports that they need to be able to get out of bed, access the community, go to work, you ostensibly isolate people."

She says many lives will be made smaller by the reforms — which will slash social and community participation supports in half.

"The support needs don't go away when the funding is cut or when the supports are removed. They just get pushed onto either systems or other people, and that means isolation."

Since it started in 2013, the cost of the scheme has ballooned, rising to $50 billion dollars this year, and projected to hit $100 billion within a decade.

The government says its overhaul will slow the scheme’s growth and save almost $38 billion over the next four years.

Greens MPs like Jordon Steele-John say the focus on financial cost has made many disabled people feel like a burden.

“Many people, during the course of this debate, while the government has been trying to push this legislation through, have shared with me that they have felt as though they are being talked about in a way that leaves them feeling like a burden, and that is just not okay.”

Health Minister Mark Butler says reining in spending growth was necessary to safeguard the scheme's financial sustainability and social license.

"This plan puts the scheme back on track, and I'm confident, secures it for decades to come," Butler said.

"It genuinely has transformed the lives of hundreds of thousands of people, and I want to continue to see that happen for decades to come. But we know also that we need to build supports for people who were never intended to be covered by the NDIS, people with more low to moderate support needs, those sorts of second-tier supports that were envisaged by the designers of this amazing reform."

title.en: Why a 52-metre SpaceX rocket ended up off the coast of Christmas Island
title.zh: 为什么一枚 52 米长的 SpaceX 火箭最终坠入圣诞岛海岸

summary.en: The rocket's arrival at the remote island caused a stir among the locals.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Elon Musk's aerospace company SpaceX has retrieved a rocket that splashed down in the Indian Ocean near Christmas Island.

The space debris was towed to the remote island, about 1,500 kilometres off north-west Western Australia, on Tuesday.

"After approx. 24 days at sea, the SpaceX Recovery team successfully guided Starship to a location just off the coast of Christmas Island," the US aerospace manufacturer and launch services company said in a social media post.

"A team of SpaceX engineers is on their way to conduct additional analysis on the vehicle in calmer waters before attempting to return it to Starbase."

Locals in the remote territory reportedly lined up along the rugged coastline to catch a glimpse of the 52-metre-long rocket as it was towed in.

Photographer Chris Bray, who usually focuses on wildlife, said it was not something he ever expected to see.

"This SpaceX Starship was towed into the protected waters around Christmas Island this morning after an unusually gentle landing in the Indian Ocean almost a month ago left it unexpectedly floating and potentially recoverable instead of the usual explosion!" he said on an Instagram post on Tuesday.

Bray's aerial photos show the mostly black-coloured rocket being towed by cable attached to two large ships.

The rocket, which has three large and three small rocket nozzles, appears to have lost some of its outer coating, but was otherwise intact.

The SpaceX website said the company's Starship spacecraft and super heavy rocket were a reusable transport system designed to carry crew and cargo into "orbit, the moon, Mars and beyond".

In 2023, a large gold-coloured dome-like object was found on a beach about 250km north of Perth.

The Australian Space Agency later concluded it was an expended third stage of a polar satellite launch vehicle operated by the Indian Space Research Organisation.

In 1979, parts of NASA's Skylab space station crashed to earth near the sleepy towns of Esperance and Balladonia, triggering a global media frenzy.

title.en: Criminal networks in crosshairs as Australia and Thailand deepen ties
title.zh: 澳大利亚和泰国加深联系，犯罪网络成为焦点

summary.en: From scam syndicates to fuel security, Australia and Thailand have mapped out a closer strategic partnership.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及合一、和好与弥合分歧。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The leaders of Australia and Thailand have agreed to step up joint efforts to tackle transnational crime, while also pledging to elevate defence and trade ties.

Thailand prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul, in his first visit to Australia since he became leader in late 2025, met with his counterpart Anthony Albanese in Canberra on Wednesday.

The pair agreed to bolster mutual commitments to handle transnational crime, including tasking their law-enforcement agencies to "disrupt increasingly sophisticated global criminal networks", they said in a joint statement.

The nations will also elevate their security relationship by committing to a biannual meeting of defence ministers.

In a boost for Australia's fuel security, Albanese said his counterpart had made the "generous offer" of access to jet fuel, as energy markets experience supply-chain shocks as a result of the US-led war on Iran.

"Building on the strong economic ties is a top priority for my government," he told reporters.

"Times of uncertainty call for greater global cooperation between partners who are reliable and dependable, and friends."

In 2027, Australia and Thailand will mark 75 years since diplomatic relations were established between the two countries.

Anutin said: "I'm confident that our strategic partnership will remain an enduring foundation for Thailand and Australia ... and bring our countries and peoples even closer together."

"I extend my sincere appreciation once again to my dear Prime Minister Albanese and the Australian people for their warm hospitality."

The bid to crack down on transnational crime comes after Thailand tries to alleviate its reputation for being a hotspot for grey money — illicit capital that crosses borders.

The nation is an international hub for online scam work which fleeces millions of dollars from Australians each year.

Vulnerable Thai locals are often imprisoned by criminal syndicates on the outskirts of Bangkok to run the centres.

The Australian Federal Police was involved in a 2025 investigation that led to the arrest of five Australians, as well as United Kingdom, Canadian and South African nationals, operating a scam Bangkok "boiler room".

That announcement also came hours after Thai police confirmed the cause of death of a Thai woman allegedly murdered by an Australian man in June.

The Thai teenager, Tunchanok Donhomla, was allegedly suffocated, according to a police autopsy report seen by the ABC.

Thai police told ABC News that, on the basis of evidence collected, they now believed the investigation was reaching its completion.

title.en: Labor reveals super increase position amid 'predatory' practices crackdown
title.zh: 工党透露在打击“掠夺性”行为中超级增加立场

summary.en: The government drew a line on compulsory superannuation as it unveiled tougher consumer protections.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Labor will not increase how much superannuation employers must pay workers, instead focusing on reforms to stamp out "predatory" practices used to lure people to put retirement savings into risky investments.

The superannuation guarantee rate — the minimum percentage of a worker's earnings that employers must pay into a retirement fund — is 12 per cent, and there have been calls within Labor to raise the rate to 15 per cent.

While rebuffing the need to increase the guarantee rate, the government has doubled down on its defence of the superannuation system amid calls from One Nation to allow workers to withdraw funds before retirement to help pay off mortgages.

"There's no plans to lift the super guarantee," Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino, who unveiled the long-awaited consumer protection reforms on Wednesday, told ABC's Radio National.

He said raising the rate to 12 per cent was something Labor had long pushed for and that was now "putting people in a very strong position" for retirement.

Mulino detailed the long-awaited crackdown on predatory practices in an address to the National Press Club on Wednesday, after the high-profile collapses of First Guardian and Shield Master Funds in 2024 and 2025 stripped an estimated 12,000 Australians of their retirement savings.

One Nation has pushed to loosen rules around early access, while the government ruled out any rise to the compulsory super guarantee on Wednesday morning.

The reforms target "lead generators" — operators who use social media, online ads and cold calls to funnel people's retirement into high-risk schemes.

Unlicensed real-time communication about superannuation will be banned, and licensees will be required to take reasonable steps to ensure lead generation activities comply with legal requirements.

The anti‑hawking regime will also be bolstered, with stronger consent requirements, a narrower exemption for financial advisers to existing clients, and harsher penalties for breaches.

Mulino said the reforms were designed to strengthen consumer protections and disrupt "predatory and inappropriate behaviour" that led to the collapse of the Shield and First Guardian funds.

"Lead generators reaching out to these people in unsolicited ways, undertaking highly manipulative interactions to convince them that their super products were not performing well or were inappropriate, and then manipulating them into inappropriate products for them," Mulino told ABC radio on Wednesday morning.

title.zh: “我们让我们的合作伙伴和家人失望了”：停赛的悉尼天鹅队球员打破沉默

summary.en: The club said the five players — who were named earlier on Wednesday — have been suspended for a breach of standards for being out late.

body.en:
The five Sydney Swans players stood down after the club found they had breached its standards on the night they were linked to a sexual assault investigation have broken their silence for the first time.

"We are deeply sorry to everyone involved," reads a statement posted to the Sydney Swans website and attributed to all five players.

"We know we have let down our partners and families, members, supporters, teammates, the AFLW team, corporate partners and everyone at the Club and in the wider community."

"We accept the Club sanction and apologise for the impact this has had on those involved."

Sydney Swans chairman Andrew Pridham earlier apologised to the club's fans and corporate partners over the conduct of the five players.

But he did not apologise to the women affected in the incident, confirming the club had made no contact with them as it was a "police matter".

Pridham and Sydney Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich fronted media on Wednesday afternoon, hours after the club confirmed Riley Bice, Nick Blakey, Isaac Heeney, James Jordon and Chad Warner would not be considered for selection for the remainder of the season, including the finals.

The sanctions follow an incident at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne that is being investigated by Victoria Police as an alleged sexual assault.

Five players were linked to the investigation and have not been arrested or charged.

However, they said the sanctions were in response to their own "standards breach" — including staying out late, drinking, and "bringing women back to the hotel" — and independent of the Victoria Police investigation.

Asked directly whether the club had apologised to the women involved, Pavlich said the club would not be reaching out.

"It's a police matter, so we're not going to interfere with that by reaching out to them," Pavlich said on Wednesday afternoon.

"We are deeply concerned about their welfare and the wellbeing of those women and we offer as much support as we can."

But Pridham's own apology, delivered at the top of the press conference, was directed elsewhere.

He offered a "sincere apology to the community, to our many fans, our corporate partners, who've been amazingly supportive of us and understanding that we are attempting to deal with this matter as quickly as we can, as honestly as we can".

Pavlich said the club's AFLW team — who play a double-header alongside the men's side this weekend — were "deeply disappointed" by the incident and that "their welfare is of the utmost importance to us".
